🚨 *new alert — needs human*  (score: 5)
Channel: alert-system  •  bug-type guess: unknown  •  alerts in group: 1

Owning team (would tag — not tagged): `Admin` (`@admin` / `#team-admin`)

Symptoms:
  - DD monitor 299603201 "[Admin][ClassicMethod][P2] P95 latency high (classic/method)" fired at 01:49:42Z.
  - Re-query of p95:trace.aspnet.request{service:classic/method,env:prod} confirms a real, sustained breach: 37 of 150 sampled points exceeded the 10.0 threshold, spanning ~16 minutes (01:45:20Z-02:01:20Z), averaging 52.4 (peak 257.36), then dropped to a sub-3 baseline for the rest of the window.
  - 0 error logs for service:classic in the surrounding 40 minutes -- latency-only symptom.
  - Rejected a spurious KB match: match_kb.py hit `ki-classic-clb-to-alb-ssl-redirect-loss` only on the bare word "Classic" in the monitor name; that entry documents an unrelated, already-resolved sign-in outage from a CLB->ALB migration. Investigated fresh instead.

Trace IDs: none captured (metric-only investigation, no APM trace pull)
Likely cause: unidentified transient latency degradation on Classic (MethodUIClassic), self-recovered, no root cause pinpointed this cycle
Suggested next action: monitor for recurrence; if this shape repeats, file a defect and pull APM traces during the next occurrence to identify the slow downstream call

🚨 *new alert — needs human*  (score: 6)
Channel: alert-system  •  bug-type guess: unknown  •  alerts in group: 1

Owning team (would tag — not tagged): `Admin` (`@admin` / `#team-admin`)

Symptoms:
  - DD monitor 299544656 "[Admin][Gateway][P3] 4xx spike (gateway)" fired at 10:32:57Z -- 2nd occurrence of this exact shape (1st: 2026-07-06, docs/investigations/2026-07-06-93e0be211df17711.md).
  - Both occurrences show an isolated 20-40 second burst carrying nearly the entire spike (today: 1613+1421 across two adjacent buckets; yesterday: 2883 in one bucket) against a 1-11/bucket baseline, both around ~10:16-10:33Z, both self-recovering within about a minute.
  - Max rolling 15-min sum today: 3093 (vs >2000 threshold, ratio 0.55).
  - DD Logs returns 0 entries for service:gateway both days (known visibility gap); this cycle's ES aggregate returned 1526 total docs in the window but an inconclusive (empty) Level.keyword breakdown -- could not identify the specific client/route/account behind either burst.
  - Given 2 consistent occurrences, wrote a new known-issues.json entry (`ki-2026-07-07-gateway-4xx-spike-monitor-noise`) this cycle so a 3rd occurrence is recognized without re-deriving from scratch.

Trace IDs: none captured (DD Logs empty for this service both days; ES breakdown inconclusive)
Likely cause: isolated, self-recovering 4xx burst on the gateway (Ocelot reverse-proxy) -- possibly a client retry storm, bot/scraper burst, or a brief JWT-cache-miss hiccup; not confirmed either way due to the logging visibility gap
Suggested next action: monitor; recommend closing the DD-Logs visibility gap for service:gateway so a 3rd occurrence can actually identify the responsible client/route
